name: Acute myeloid leukemia

meta.title: AML in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults; newly diagnosed (fit and unfit pathways) and relapsed/refractory settings. Acute promyelocytic leukemia is excluded: PML-RARA defines a different disease with its own arm family (ATRA/arsenic, no routine allo-HCT in CR1) and is split to its own catalog row per the subtype granularity rule.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application showing how an in silico engine gates, models, and ranks treatment decisions across the adult non-APL AML journey - fitness-driven frontline branching, molecularly gated add-ons, the CR/MRD checkpoint, and the transplant frontier - for clinicians, patients, and caregivers. Scope boundaries invoked: APL is a separate spec; complication and supportive-event management (febrile neutropenia, tumor lysis) renders as co-interventions, never as ranked arms; dosing and order sets are out of scope. Trial age ranges are recorded in each arm's anchor but deliberately…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022); ICC 2022 acknowledged where the two diverge
meta.response: ELN 2022 response criteria (CR, CRi, CRh, MRD)

stages.label: Confirm the diagnosis
stages.question: Is this AML - and is it the AML this trainer covers?
stages.decision: Confirm >=20% marrow blasts (WHO-HAEM5) and exclude PML-RARA before anything else.

stages.label: Risk and fitness
stages.question: What biology is this, and what can this patient tolerate?
stages.decision: Resolve FLT3/NPM1/IDH panel and ELN 2022 risk; judge induction fitness.

stages.label: Frontline plan
stages.question: Which induction (or lower-intensity) strategy, for this biology and this fitness?
stages.decision: Rank eligible frontline arms; show gated arms with reasons.

stages.label: Response checkpoint
stages.question: Did induction work - and how deep is the remission?
stages.decision: Read the day 21-28 marrow; then MRD after count recovery/consolidation.

stages.label: Consolidation and transplant
stages.question: Consolidate with chemotherapy and maintenance, or take the transplant?
stages.decision: Weigh relapse-risk reduction against transplant-related mortality, per ELN risk and MRD.

stages.label: Relapsed / refractory
stages.question: What now - targeted, intensive, low-intensity, or comfort?
stages.decision: Rank salvage arms by the same rules: mutation gates first, fitness second, honesty always.

stages.label: Trial matching
stages.question: Which open studies fit this patient today?
stages.decision: Evaluate encodable criteria three-state: match, blocked, needs-data.

stages.label: Data readiness
stages.question: Which missing result would change the answer most?
stages.decision: Rank artifacts by live value-of-information flips.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Age is a continuous hazard modifier here, not a hard gate; trial age ranges are recorded on each arm card instead.
Patient.helpPatient: Age changes the odds but does not by itself close any door in this trainer.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: ECOG 2 and >=3 carry cited hazard modifiers; the fitness judgment below is the eligibility switch.
Patient.helpPatient: How much daily activity is possible right now - it shifts the numbers.

Patient.label: Induction fitness
Patient.help: Composite judgment (VIALE-A-style: age >=75 or disqualifying comorbidity). Flips the entire frontline arm family.
Patient.helpPatient: Whether intensive hospital chemotherapy is a safe option - if not, there is a well-proven gentler pathway.

Patient.label: Comorbidity burden
Patient.help: High burden applies a cited hazard modifier and typically informs the fitness judgment.
Patient.helpPatient: Other health problems that make treatment harder on the body.

Diagnostic gates.label: Marrow blasts
Diagnostic gates.help: WHO-HAEM5 requires >=20% blasts absent an AML-defining lesion; below threshold the workup routes to MDS/MPN pathways.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: The share of immature cells in the bone marrow - it defines whether this is acute leukemia.

Diagnostic gates.label: PML-RARA (APL screen)
Diagnostic gates.help: APL is a medical emergency and a different disease (ATRA/arsenic pathway, own guideline section). Positive hard-reroutes out of this trainer.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: A quick test for a special leukemia type that is treated completely differently - and urgently.

Molecular panel.label: FLT3 status
Molecular panel.help: Flips the frontline family: ITD opens midostaurin and quizartinib add-ons; TKD opens midostaurin only (QuANTUM-First enrolled ITD only). Pending blocks ranking per ELN 2022.
Molecular panel.helpPatient: A gene change that opens targeted add-on drugs - worth waiting a few days for.

Molecular panel.label: NPM1
Molecular panel.help: ELN risk input; in relapse, NPM1 mutation is a menin-inhibitor (revumenib) selector.
Molecular panel.helpPatient: Another gene result that helps sort risk and, at relapse, can open a targeted pill.

Molecular panel.label: IDH1
Molecular panel.help: Mutation opens ivosidenib-azacitidine for the unfit patient (AGILE).
Molecular panel.helpPatient: If this gene is changed, a targeted pill can be added to the gentler pathway.

Molecular panel.label: IDH2
Molecular panel.help: At relapse, opens enasidenib - which improved responses but failed its randomized OS endpoint (IDHENTIFY); the card carries that flag.
Molecular panel.helpPatient: A gene change that can open another targeted pill at relapse, with honestly mixed trial results.

Molecular panel.label: KMT2A rearrangement
Molecular panel.help: At relapse, opens the menin inhibitor revumenib (AUGMENT-101).
Molecular panel.helpPatient: A chromosome change that can open one of the newest targeted pills at relapse.

Risk.label: ELN 2022 risk
Risk.help: Derived from cytogenetics + the molecular panel per ELN 2022. Drives the relapse-risk prior, the transplant conditional, and the favorable-risk gemtuzumab add-on. Pending blocks ranking.
Risk.helpPatient: The overall risk group from the chromosome and gene tests - it shapes both the plan and the transplant question.

Risk.label: Disease history
Risk.help: Secondary/therapy-related AML applies a cited hazard modifier and opens CPX-351 substitution for the fit patient.
Risk.helpPatient: Whether the leukemia arose on its own or after earlier blood disease or cancer treatment.

On treatment.label: Post-induction marrow
On treatment.help: CR unlocks the consolidation arms (allo-HCT conditional on risk, CC-486 maintenance); residual disease routes toward the refractory pathway.
On treatment.helpPatient: The check a few weeks into treatment that tells us whether the first round worked.

On treatment.label: Measurable residual disease
On treatment.help: ELN 2022 treats MRD as a routing input: positivity raises the modeled relapse risk that pushes the transplant discussion.
On treatment.helpPatient: A very sensitive test for leftover leukemia cells even when the marrow looks clean.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Where you are.label: Your state (optional)
Where you are.help: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.
Where you are.helpPatient: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.

Newly diagnosed.name: 7+3 induction, then HiDAC consolidation
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: prolonged cytopenias; induction mortality risk rises with age
Newly diagnosed.patient: The classic intensive hospital chemotherapy, aiming for remission and possibly cure.

Newly diagnosed.name: 7+3 + midostaurin (FLT3-mutated)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: adds cytopenias, rash, QT monitoring to 7+3
Newly diagnosed.patient: The same intensive chemotherapy plus a targeted pill matched to the FLT3 gene change.

Newly diagnosed.name: 7+3 + quizartinib (FLT3-ITD)
Newly diagnosed.patient: Intensive chemotherapy plus a targeted pill specific to the ITD form of the FLT3 change, continued up to three years.

Newly diagnosed.name: 7+3 + gemtuzumab ozogamicin (favorable risk)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN option (favorable risk); FDA 2017 re-approval after 2010 withdrawal
Newly diagnosed.patient: An antibody-drug added to chemotherapy for the most favorable gene profiles - a drug that was withdrawn once and came back at a safer dose.

Newly diagnosed.name: CPX-351 (liposomal 7+3, secondary/t-AML)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: similar profile to 7+3 with longer count recovery
Newly diagnosed.patient: The same two chemotherapy drugs packaged together in a way that works better for leukemias that grew out of earlier marrow disease.

Newly diagnosed.name: Azacitidine + venetoclax (unfit)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: febrile neutropenia 42%, grade >=3 thrombocytopenia 45%; tumor-lysis ramp-up
Newly diagnosed.patient: The proven gentler pathway: a monthly injection cycle plus a daily pill, mostly outpatient.

Newly diagnosed.name: Ivosidenib + azacitidine (IDH1-mutated, unfit)
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the IDH1 gene change: a targeted daily pill added to the monthly injections.

Newly diagnosed.name: Azacitidine alone
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN option when venetoclax is not tolerated/available
Newly diagnosed.patient: The injection cycles alone - gentler still, with honestly modest trial results.

Newly diagnosed.name: Allogeneic transplant consolidation (CR1, intermediate/adverse)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: 2-yr non-relapse mortality 9% vs 2% (ETAL-1) - disclosed verbatim on this card per honesty constraint; chronic GVHD risk
Newly diagnosed.patient: Replacing the marrow with a donor's - the strongest anti-relapse tool, with real upfront risks the card states plainly.

Newly diagnosed.name: Oral azacitidine maintenance (CR after intensive chemo)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN option (maintenance post-intensive when not transplanted); FDA approved 2020
Newly diagnosed.patient: A maintenance pill after remission for those not going to transplant - it measurably extends remission and survival.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always an option; ASCO palliative care integration
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: focused on symptom relief; transfusion support continues
Newly diagnosed.patient: Full attention on feeling as well as possible for as long as possible, without anti-leukemia drugs.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Gilteritinib (FLT3-mutated relapse)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A daily targeted pill that beat another round of intensive chemotherapy in a head-to-head trial.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Revumenib (KMT2A-rearranged / NPM1-mutated relapse)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN option (KMT2Ar R/R); NPM1 indication confirmed FDA 2025-10-24 (Revuforj second indication - verified 2026-08-24)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: One of the newest targeted pills, for two specific gene profiles; response data are strong, survival data still maturing - the card says which is which.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Ziftomenib (NPM1-mutated relapse)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FDA approved R/R NPM1-mutated AML (Komzifti 2025-11-13, verified 2026-08-24); NCCN AML inclusion status: confirm at next refresh
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase II single-arm registration cohort (N=92); overall-population median OS read firsthand from the trial publication - no comparator arm exists
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: One of the newest targeted pills for the NPM1 gene change, approved late 2025; response and survival data come from a single-arm trial with no comparison group, so the survival number is an absolute figure for everyone treated and cannot be read as a gain over another option.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Enasidenib (IDH2-mutated relapse)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A targeted pill for the IDH2 change that improves responses but did not extend survival in its randomized trial - shown here with exactly that honesty.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Intensive salvage (FLAG-IDA/MEC class) bridging to transplant
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN option (fit R/R) as transplant bridge
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Another round of intensive hospital chemotherapy, chosen when the goal is a second remission strong enough to carry into transplant.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Low-intensity salvage (HMA-based)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Gentler outpatient treatment aiming to control the leukemia and protect quality of life.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always an option; ASCO palliative care integration
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Full attention on comfort and time that feels like your own.

secondary/therapy-related history routes CPX-351; favorable cytogenetics routes GO

refs.label: THE WRONG-POPULATION GUARD: Dohner et al., 'Genetic risk classification for adults with AML receiving less-intensive therapies: the 2024 ELN recommendations' (Blood 2024 - PMID 39133932, pubmed-eutils-verified 2026-08-27). ELN 2022 was derived in intensively treated adults; the 2024-NI classification exists precisely because unfit/ven-aza patients need their own risk model.

honesty: Registry wins for status; the peer-reviewed paper wins for numbers; both are logged.
Transplant cards disclose ETAL-1 verbatim: 2-yr non-relapse mortality 9% vs 2%, and overall survival was not superior to consolidation with transplant-at-relapse.
The azacitidine-alone card leads with AZA-AML-001's non-significant primary OS analysis (HR 0.85, p=0.10), not the favorable censored sensitivity analysis.
ALFA-0701's primary endpoint is EFS; the gemtuzumab card never presents OS as its headline claim, and carries the 2010-withdrawal/2017-re-approval reversal flag.
IDHENTIFY failed its OS endpoint; the enasidenib card leads with that, not the response rates.

Medians labeled 'teaching approximation' are derived from verified fractional-survival anchors via the exponential family (or explicitly placeholder, e.g. revumenib pending its OS readout) and are flagged in-product.
Unverified statuses never carry today's date.
Comfort-focused care is a modeled arm in every setting.
Trial age ranges are recorded on arm cards, not silently converted into hard gates.
gates: apl must be excluded for the non-APL AML pathway
marrowBlasts >= 20 required for the AML diagnosis
flt3 and eln risk must be resulted before frontline ranking
consolidation routing waits for the post-induction marrow and MRD
care: High-volume acute-leukemia center (24/7 blood bank, ICU, rapid molecular turnaround)
Targeted-therapy monitoring program (QTc, differentiation syndrome) for the relapse menu
Community-deliverable maintenance (the honest inverse for this corner)

surveillance.cadence: CBC every 1-3 months per guideline; marrow on count abnormalities
